blocks.text: Account onboarding in AI Security enables organizations to establish a secure, governed foundation for managing and monitoring AI application usage. By integrating user identities, cloud environments, and security policies from the outset, organizations gain immediate visibility and control over how AI tools are accessed and used across the enterprise.

AI Security continuously monitors and scans the onboarded accounts for sensitive data and vulnerabilities, and generates issues based on data security policy violations. AI Security supports the onboarding of Amazon Web Services (AWS) accounts, Microsoft Azure subscriptions, Google Cloud Platform (GCP) projects, and SaaS applications like Microsoft Copilot Studio.
Account Onboarding in AI Security provides the following benefits:

blocks.item: Gain a unified view of all AI application usage across the organization, including SaaS applications and cloud environments.
Detect misconfigurations, vulnerabilities, potential threats that could lead to data breach.
Respond to security risks and take necessary action to prevent data breach.
Detect and restrict unauthorized AI applications automatically.

blocks.text: On the Account Onboarding page (Administration> Account Onboarding), you can do the following:

blocks.item: View metrics from the following perspectives:
Total Environments: The total number of environments that have been added and configured across all integrations.
Healthy Integrations: Integrations for which all required permission checks and access validations have passed.
Unhealthy Integrations: Integrations where one or more permission checks, access validations, or configuration checks have failed or reported issues.
Pending Configuration: Integrations with one or more environments that are added but still require configuration to be completed.
Click + Add New to start onboarding Cloud Providers or SaaS Platforms.
Search for a specific integration in the Configured Integrations table.
Apply filters to view specific data.
Show or hide columns of the table.
Show or hide filters of the table
View a list of accounts that are onboarded. For each account you can view the following:
Integration Alias: The display name for the integration as configured in the system. Click the integration name to view additional details
While the onboarding process is in progress or if AI Security has encountered issues, you can view the issue or paused step and resume onboarding.
When the onboarding process is completed successfully, you can view the following tabs:
Overview: The onboarding status and the orchestrator details.
Subscriptions, Projects, Accounts, or Environments (based on the cloud account or SaaS application): Details of the onboarded cloud account.
Issues: The issues encountered while onboarding.
Roles and Templates: The roles created while onboarding and templates generated by AI Security.
Manage the cloud accounts:
Monitoring & Autodetection: Add new accounts to the monitoring scope and enable autodetection.
Business Units Mapping: Assign a different business unit to the account.
On Demand Validation: Validate the onboarded accounts.
Manage Regions: Select regions that must be monitored and scanned or configure regions to deploy scanning resources for custom network configuration.
Manage Custom Tags: Add, edit, or delete custom tags.
Manage Notification Emails: Add email addresses of the recipient to be notified of any configuration or permissions issues while onboarding.
Managing Orchestrator Network (Custom): Configure the orchestrator network (applicable only if the AI Security Connection Status is failed). To learn more, see Viewing Orchestrator Status.
Configure New Orchestrator (Zscaler): Change the orchestrator account.
Delete Account: Delete or offboard an account.
Manage SaaS Applications:
Add New Account/Environment: Add new account or environment.
Update Credentials: Update credentials.
Delete Integration: Delete integration.
Provider: The service the integration connects to, e.g., AWS, Azure, GCP, Copilot Studio, etc.
Accounts: The number of accounts, tenants, or environments onboarded under the integration.
Business Units: The organizational groups associated with the integration.
Health Status: The overall integration health based on validation checks, e.g., Passed, Pending, Needs Attention, etc.
Orchestrator Config Status: The configuration state of the orchestrator or connector used to run the integration, e.g., Successfully Configured, Pending Configuration, Needs Attention).
Issues: A summary or count of detected problems affecting the integration, e.g., failed checks, missing permissions, configuration errors.
Actions: Available actions are as follows:
Cloud Service Providers: Modify Integration or Delete Integration.
SaaS Applications: Add New Account/Environment, Update Credentials, or Delete Integration.
